title: MAKING AN APPOINTMENT WITH MYSELF
passages: The early mornings became a place I could return to. Sound before the noise of the day. Movement before everyone else's demands. Heat, quiet, and a little time to notice how I felt.

I started describing self-care as something I had to schedule. Responsibilities were always going to fill the available space. If I wanted a life with energy left for creativity and connection, I needed to make room for myself inside it. The ritual began before sunrise.

reflections.prompt: Where do you disappear from your own schedule?
Find ten minutes in tomorrow’s day that can belong to you. What would you like to do with them?
Put those ten minutes on your calendar. Make the appointment small enough to keep.
